segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: And today we're bringing you another lesson on our sports series.
segments.zh: 今天，我们将为您带来关于我们的运动系列的另一个课程。
我们今天谈论的是棒球。

segments.en: So we're going to be looking at this interesting sport that is played mainly in the Caribbean and well, it's actually very popular in the United States and Japan.
segments.zh: 所以我们将关注这项主要在加勒比地区进行的有趣运动，而且它实际上在美国和日本非常受欢迎。

segments.en: And we're going to learn a bunch of baseball language, but we're also going to see how baseball has a big influence on English in general.
segments.zh: 我们将学习一堆棒球语言，但我们也将看到棒球对英语有很大的影响。

segments.en: So we're going to learn a lot of great things today.
segments.zh: 所以我们今天要学到很多很棒的东西。

segments.en: So why don't we start and listen to our dialogue?
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不开始并倾听我们的对话呢？

segments.en: Hello baseball fans and welcome back to today's game.
segments.zh: 各位棒球迷好，欢迎回到今天的比赛。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields and of course I am here once again with the man that seals the deal Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我是瑞克·菲尔兹，今天还是由我的老搭档鲍勃·科普兰和我一起解说。

segments.en: It's a beautiful day to see two world-class teams face each other and fight for their right to be called champions.
segments.zh: 今天天气绝佳，两支世界级球队将在这里争夺冠军。

segments.en: Well, the national anthem has just been sung and the umpire has started the game.
segments.zh: 国歌刚刚奏完，主审宣布比赛开始。

segments.en: Roger Vargas is up at bat.
segments.zh: 罗杰·巴尔加斯上场击球。

segments.en: Pitcher winds up and strike one.
Very nice curve ball by the pitcher.
segments.zh: 投手这记曲球投得漂亮。

segments.en: The catcher gives him the sign.
He winds up and Vargas gets a line drive.
segments.zh: 投手再次扬臂，巴尔加斯击出一记平飞球！

segments.en: The players are scrambling to get the ball.
Vargas gets to first base and he's still going.
segments.zh: 巴尔加斯跑上一垒，还在继续冲。

segments.en: The outfielder throws it to second.
We have a runner on third and up at bat is Brian Okami.
segments.zh: 三垒有跑者，现在上场击球的是布赖恩·冈美。

segments.en: That puts this team ahead by two as we are at the bottom of the fifth inning here at Ritchie Stadium.
segments.zh: 现在是里奇球场的第五局下半，这支球队凭这一球领先两分。

segments.en: Well, a pretty exciting game there at Richie Stadium.
segments.zh: 好吧，在里奇体育场举行的一场非常令人兴奋的比赛。

segments.en: And we have some interesting players, Roger Vargas and Brian Okami.
segments.zh: 我们有一些有趣的球员，罗杰·巴尔加斯和布赖恩·奥卡米。

segments.en: So well, we saw some great words and well, it's time for us to take a look at them now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们看到了一些很棒的词，好吧，是时候让我们在语言外卖中看看它们了。

segments.en: We're going to look at some common sports and baseball words here.
segments.zh: 我们将在这里查看一些常见的运动和棒球单词。

segments.en: Now, the first phrase, we'll hear this almost at any sort of international sports event, right?
segments.zh: 现在，第一个短语，我们将在任何类型的国际体育赛事中听到这一点，对吧？

segments.en: So, this is a song, right?
It's the song that you sing about your country and many people confuse it, right?
segments.zh: 这是你唱的关于你的国家的歌，很多人都把它弄糊涂了，对吧？

segments.en: A lot of people might say national hymn.
Because in some languages, it might be like a hymn, like literally translating.
segments.zh: 因为在某些语言中，它可能就像一首赞美诗，就像字面翻译一样。

segments.en: But in English, it's called the national anthem.
segments.zh: 但在英语中，它被称为国歌。

segments.en: So, what about our next word?
segments.zh: 那么，我们的下一个词呢？

segments.en: Well, we were talking about the pitcher.
And now, this is one of the players on the baseball team and his job is to?
segments.zh: 而现在，这是棒球队的球员之一，他的工作是？

segments.en: To throw the ball really fast.
So that the guy can hit it with the bat.
segments.zh: 这样男生就可以用球拍打它。

segments.en: Now, the interesting thing is that the baseball commentator said the pitcher winds up.
segments.zh: 现在，有趣的是棒球评论员说投手结束了。

segments.en: Well, let me paint you a picture.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我给你画一幅画。

segments.en: And you're turning, turning, and turning the clock to wind it up, to get it ready to go.
segments.zh: 你正在转动，转动，转动时钟以将其收起，让它准备好去。

segments.en: And the pitcher is doing the same sort of thing, bringing his arm back behind him, getting ready to throw the ball.
segments.zh: 投手也在做同样的事情，把他的手臂放回他身后，准备把球扔出去。

segments.en: So, that is to wind up.
So, you can use this word not only in baseball, but for other things that require you to do this action.
segments.zh: 因此，您不仅可以在棒球中使用这个词，还可以用于需要您执行此操作的其他事情。

segments.en: To turn something and get it ready to have lots of power.
segments.zh: 转动一些东西并准备好拥有大量的力量。

segments.en: Or maybe like a music box.
segments.zh: 或者可能像一个音乐盒。

segments.en: Well, Roger Vargas hit a line drive.
segments.zh: 好吧，罗杰·巴尔加斯击中了一个线驱动器。

segments.en: So, what is a line drive?
segments.zh: 那么，什么是线路驱动器呢？

segments.en: Well, it's a term from baseball.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是棒球的一个术语。

segments.en: And when you hit a line drive, you hit the ball sort of low on towards the ground, and it travels along the outside of the field.
segments.zh: 当你击中一个线驱动时，你会将球击向地面，然后沿着场地外侧移动。

segments.en: So, the ball basically travels along the foul line.
segments.zh: 所以，球基本上沿着罚球线传播。
所以，这是一个线路驱动器。

segments.en: And so, the players on the field were scrambling to get the ball.
segments.zh: 于是，球场上的球员们都在争先恐后地拿到球。

segments.en: Now, we know scrambled eggs from one of our lessons.
segments.zh: 现在，我们从我们的一课中知道了炒鸡蛋。

segments.en: But the verb to scramble means to move quickly in a disorganized way to do something.
segments.zh: 但是动词 to scramble 的意思是以杂乱无章的方式快速移动做某事。

segments.en: So, the players are moving very fast, trying to get the ball, but they're not doing it very well.
segments.zh: 所以，球员们的移动速度非常快，试图拿到球，但他们做得并不好。

segments.en: And you can use this in other ways, right?
segments.zh: 你可以以其他方式使用它，对吧？

segments.en: For example, we can say, the people are scrambling to buy their tickets for the concert.
segments.zh: 例如，我们可以说，人们正在争先恐后地购买音乐会的门票。

segments.en: Or, I'm going on vacation tomorrow and I'm scrambling to get everything ready.
segments.zh: 或者，我明天要去度假，我正争先恐后地准备好一切。

segments.en: It's a very good term that you can use also in your daily life.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常好的术语，您也可以在日常生活中使用。

segments.en: And what about our last word for today on Language Takeaway?
segments.zh: 我们今天关于语言外卖的最后一个词呢？

segments.en: Well, they were in the fifth inning of the game.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们在比赛的第五局。

segments.en: And it just means the period of play.
segments.zh: 它只是意味着游戏的时期。

segments.en: So, we learned, for example, that in soccer you have two halves.
segments.zh: 例如，我们了解到，在足球中你有两半。

segments.en: Or, in hockey, you have three periods.
segments.zh: 或者，在曲棍球中，您有三个时期。

segments.en: And in baseball, you have nine innings.
segments.zh: 在棒球比赛中，你有九局。

segments.en: So, some interesting sports and baseball vocabulary.
segments.zh: 所以，一些有趣的运动和棒球词汇。

segments.en: Now, I think it'll help us to hear this again slower.
segments.zh: 现在，我认为它会帮助我们慢慢听到这一点。

segments.en: So, let's listen to the dialogue.
Hello, baseball fans, and welcome back to today's game.
segments.zh: 你好，棒球迷，欢迎回到今天的比赛。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields, and of course, I am here once again with the man that seals the deal, Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Rick Fields，当然，我再次和达成交易的人 Bob Copeland 在一起。

segments.en: It's a beautiful day to see two world-class teams face each other and fight for their right to be called champions.
segments.zh: 今天天气绝佳，两支世界级球队将在这里争夺冠军。

segments.en: Well, the national anthem has just been sung, and the umpire has started the game.
segments.zh: 好吧，国歌刚刚被唱，裁判已经开始了比赛。

segments.en: Roger Vargas is up at bat.
segments.zh: 罗杰·巴尔加斯上场击球。

segments.en: The pitcher winds up and strike one.
A very nice curveball by the pitcher.
segments.zh: 投手一个非常漂亮的曲线球。

segments.en: The catcher gives him the sign.
He winds up, and Vargas gets a line drive.
segments.zh: 他结束了，巴尔加斯得到了一个线路驱动。

segments.en: The players are scrambling to get the ball.
Vargas gets to first base, and he's still going.
segments.zh: 巴尔加斯进入一垒，他还在继续。

segments.en: The outfielder throws it to second.
We have a runner on third, and up at bat is Brian Okami.
segments.zh: 我们有一个跑步者在第三名，在击球时是布赖恩·奥卡米。

segments.en: That puts this team ahead by two, as we are at the bottom of the fifth inning here at Ritchie Stadium.
segments.zh: 这让这支球队领先了两个，因为我们在里奇体育场的第五局的底部。

segments.en: All right, so as we said, there are a lot of English terms that come from baseball, but we use them in business context or in your daily life, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，正如我们所说，有很多来自棒球的英语术语，但我们在商业环境或您的日常生活中使用它们，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, why don't we look at those now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 是的，我们为什么不看看现在在 Fluency Builder 中的那些。

segments.en: All right, so the first phrase that we have is, up to bat.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们有的第一个短语是，直到击球。

segments.en: So literally, in this dialogue, it means the guy is standing on home plate, ready to hit the ball, right?
segments.zh: 所以从字面上看，在这个对话中，这意味着这家伙站在本垒板上，准备好击球，对吧？

segments.en: He has the bat, and he's ready to hit it.
segments.zh: 他有球棒，他已经准备好击球了。

segments.en: But what about in other contexts?
So for example, you can be at a meeting, and maybe it's your turn to talk.
segments.zh: 例如，你可以参加会议，也许轮到你说话了。

segments.en: Your boss will say, okay, Erica, you're up to bat.
segments.zh: 你的老板会说，好吧，埃里卡，你快要打击了。

segments.en: Okay, so it means sort of like it's your turn.
segments.zh: 好吧，这意味着有点像轮到你了。

segments.en: All right, so that's another term that is used in baseball, but very commonly used in other circumstances.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是棒球中使用的另一个术语，但在其他情况下非常常用。

segments.en: So we also saw in the dialogue that Roger Vegas, he hit the ball, but he missed, and that was strike one.
segments.zh: 所以我们也在对话中看到罗杰维加斯，他击球，但他错过了，那是一击。

segments.en: So in baseball, you have three strikes.
segments.zh: 所以在棒球比赛中，你有三次罢工。
在你出去之前的三次尝试。

segments.en: And so now, the same thing happens in daily life.
segments.zh: 所以现在，同样的事情发生在日常生活中。

segments.en: So if someone says, that was strike one.
segments.zh: 所以如果有人说，那就是罢工之一。

segments.en: It means you made the first mistake.
segments.zh: 这意味着你犯了第一个错误。

segments.en: And if you make two more, you will be fired, for example.
segments.zh: 例如，如果您再制作两个，您将被解雇。

segments.en: Or maybe your parents will say, okay, that wasn't nice.
segments.zh: 或者也许你的父母会说，好吧，那不好。

segments.en: And then two more times, and you'll have a timeout.
segments.zh: 然后再两次，你就会有一个超时。

segments.en: Okay, so that's also called a strike.
And the pitcher threw a curve ball.
segments.zh: 投手投出了一个曲线球。

segments.en: A curve ball is when you throw the ball, and it sort of goes in a curve.
segments.zh: 曲线球是当你扔球时，它有点弯曲。

segments.en: But how can this be used outside of baseball?
segments.zh: 但这如何在棒球之外使用呢？

segments.en: So you can say, oh, my boss threw me a curve ball today.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，哦，我的老板今天给我扔了一个曲线球。

segments.en: So he gave you an unexpected problem.
segments.zh: 所以他给了你一个意想不到的问题。

segments.en: Or something that was difficult to handle.
I'd like to hear a few more examples.
My boss threw me a curve ball today, so I have to stay and work late.
segments.zh: 我的老板今天给我扔了一个曲线球，所以我必须留下来工作到很晚。

segments.en: It was a huge curve ball when she asked me how many kids I wanted to have.
segments.zh: 当她问我想生几个孩子时，这是一个巨大的曲线球。

segments.en: How am I supposed to know?
All right, so that's basically a curve ball.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这基本上是一个曲线球。

segments.en: You can say an unexpected problem or situation.
segments.zh: 你可以说一个意想不到的问题或情况。

segments.en: And our last phrase, and probably one that you already know, home run.
segments.zh: 还有我们的最后一句话，可能是你已经知道的一句，本垒打。

segments.en: From baseball, we know that that's when you hit the ball really far.
segments.zh: 从棒球，我们知道那是你击球的时候。

segments.en: And you hit it outside of the playing area, outside the park.
segments.zh: 然后你在公园外的比赛区外击球。

segments.en: And now if you use it in a business context or in your daily life.
segments.zh: 现在，如果您在商业环境或日常生活中使用它。

segments.en: Why don't we take a listen to the examples and see if we can figure it out.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不听听这些例子，看看我们是否能弄清楚。

segments.en: Great job on that sales presentation.
segments.zh: 销售演示文稿的出色工作。

segments.en: You really hit a home run.
segments.zh: 你真的打了一个本垒打。

segments.en: Our sales team hit a home run this month by doubling our revenue.
segments.zh: 我们的销售团队本月通过将我们的收入翻了一番来达到本垒打。

segments.en: Okay, so basically a home run is a success.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上本垒打是成功的。
是的，有什么，一个很大的成就。

segments.en: So we've seen a lot of these great phrases.
segments.zh: 所以我们看到了很多这些伟大的短语。

segments.en: And as you can see, a lot of them from baseball are used in your daily life.
segments.zh: 正如您所看到的，其中很多棒球都用于您的日常生活。

segments.en: And there are many, many more.
Okay, well, why don't we hear them again in the baseball context.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们为什么不在棒球环境中再次听到他们的声音。

segments.en: And we'll listen to the dialogue one more time.
Hello baseball fans and welcome back to today's game.
segments.zh: 各位棒球迷好，欢迎回到今天的比赛。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields and of course I am here once again with the man that seals the deal Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Rick Fields，当然我又和 Bob Copeland 达成交易的人再次来到这里。

segments.en: It's a beautiful day to see two world class teams face each other and fight for their right to be called champions.
segments.zh: 这是一个美好的一天，看到两支世界级的球队面对面并为他们被称为冠军的权利而战。

segments.en: Well, the national anthem has just been sung and the umpire has started the game.
segments.zh: 国歌刚刚奏完，主审宣布比赛开始。

segments.en: Roger Vargas is up at bat.
segments.zh: 罗杰·巴尔加斯上场击球。

segments.en: Pitcher winds up and strike one.
Very nice curve ball by the pitcher.
segments.zh: 投手这记曲球投得漂亮。

segments.en: The catcher gives him the sign.
He winds up and Vargas gets a line drive.
segments.zh: 投手再次扬臂，巴尔加斯击出一记平飞球！

segments.en: The players are scrambling to get the ball.
Vargas gets to first base and he's still going.
segments.zh: 巴尔加斯跑上一垒，还在继续冲。

segments.en: The outfielder throws it to second.
We have a runner on third and up at bat is Brian Okami.
segments.zh: 三垒有跑者，现在上场击球的是布赖恩·冈美。

segments.en: That puts this team ahead by two as we are at the bottom of the fifth inning here at Ritchie Stadium.
segments.zh: 这使这支球队领先两人，因为我们在里奇体育场的第五局比赛中处于领先地位。

segments.en: So an interesting dialogue, a very interesting sport.
segments.zh: 所以一个有趣的对话，一个非常有趣的运动。

segments.en: And well, personally, I never played this as a child.
segments.zh: 好吧，就个人而言，我小时候从来没有玩过这个。

segments.en: I don't really like it too much, but it is kind of fun to go to a game and especially in the United States, have those hot dogs and all that.
segments.zh: 我不太喜欢它，但是去看比赛，尤其是在美国，拥有那些热狗等等，这很有趣。

segments.en: Well, a cultural event, a really important piece of American culture.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个文化活动，一个非常重要的美国文化片段。

segments.en: So, well, we encourage you to come to our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 因此，我们鼓励您访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: And also, of course, if you have questions or doubts, be sure to tell us.
segments.zh: 当然，如果您有任何疑问或疑问，请务必告诉我们。

segments.en: If you have any other sort of baseball related phrases, let us know about them on the website.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何其他类型的棒球相关短语，请在网站上告诉我们。

segments.en: OK, so we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们会在那里见到你们。
